questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to repair an old clock that has stopped working
Why Rob is always late for work in the mornings
How exact clock time has come to control our lives
The best watches to buy for under a hundred pounds
questions.why: They discuss what would happen if clocks stopped, and how we have become 'slaves to time'.

questions.q: Why doesn't Rob own a watch?
options: He trusts his own sense of time
He lost his last one
He uses his phone instead
He can't afford one
questions.why: Rob says, 'I rely on my internal clock – it's pretty good.'

questions.q: What is Rob's opinion about time in modern life?
options: Clocks help us relax more
People don't care about time any more
We should have more clocks in public places
We are slaves to time, with clocks on everything
questions.why: Rob says 'we're slaves to time' with digital clocks on phones, computers, microwaves and bus stops.

questions.q: How does Neil's view of time differ from Rob's?
options: He thinks clocks are unnecessary
He thinks good timekeeping is very important
He prefers to tell the time by the sun
He agrees completely with Rob
questions.why: Neil says good timekeeping is extremely important because of schedules and deadlines.

questions.q: How did people tell the time before mechanical clocks?
options: By listening to church bells only
By watching the sun, moon and stars
By counting their steps
By using pendulums
questions.why: Rob says they observed how the position of the sun, moon and stars changed.

questions.q: According to Dr Silke Ackermann, what did many societies need to know in the past?
options: The exact hour and minute
When their work meetings started
What time the shops closed
How much daylight was left or when to pray
questions.why: She says it wasn't relevant to know it's four o'clock; they needed daylight left or prayer times.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention the start of Ramadan?
options: To show that modern clocks are now accurate to the second
To say it happens on the same date every year everywhere
As an example of time still set by nature, not clocks
To explain why prayer times have changed in recent years
questions.why: He says it's calculated by the rising crescent moon, which modern timekeeping can't calculate.

questions.q: What does Dr Ackermann mean when she calls precision a 'straitjacket'?
options: Always needing exact time limits us in a harmful way
Precise clocks are uncomfortable to wear on your wrist
Exact time makes us more free to plan our days
Clocks are too expensive for most people to buy
questions.why: Neil explains she means always wanting precise time 'can limit what we do in a way that is damaging'.
